The IT Onsite Support Specialist provides hands-on Level 2 IT support at assigned business locations, serving as the local extension of Global IT teams. The role is responsible for resolving technical issues that require physical presence, maintaining site technology and operational readiness, managing IT assets, and supporting employee onboarding and offboarding. This position also provides hands-on assistance to Network, Platform, Security, and Workplace teams and coordinates with remote teams and external vendors when additional support is required.

We are looking for a hands-on IT professional who combines strong technical troubleshooting skills with a customer-focused mindset and the ability to work independently in a business environment. The ideal candidate takes ownership of issues, communicates effectively with users and technical teams, and is comfortable working across different areas of IT to deliver reliable onsite support.

**Your Responsibilities

**

• Deliver Level 2 onsite support for hardware, software, connectivity, mobile devices, printers, meeting rooms, and workplace technology.

• Resolve incidents and service requests through ServiceNow while meeting established service levels and maintaining clear ticket documentation.

• Maintain site IT readiness by ensuring end-user devices, meeting room technology, printers, network equipment, and other local technology remain operational.

• Execute hands-on activities for Global IT teams, including equipment installation, replacement, troubleshooting, cabling, rack and stack, reboots, and other physical infrastructure activities.

• Manage IT assets and inventory, including receiving, deployment, recovery, stock management, audits, and lifecycle activities.

• Support employee onboarding and offboarding by preparing, deploying, recovering, reimaging, and securing IT equipment.

• Coordinate with remote IT teams and vendors to resolve complex technical issues and complete activities requiring additional expertise or external resources.

• Support IT projects, site surveys, office moves, infrastructure activities, and other initiatives requiring onsite technical presence.

• Maintain knowledge articles, procedures, and documentation while identifying opportunities to improve onsite support processes and service quality.

**What You Bring

**

• Bring 3–5 years of experience in IT support, desktop support, or a related technical role.

• Demonstrate experience providing onsite enterprise IT support and resolving hardware and software issues.

• Apply strong knowledge of Windows, Microsoft 365, mobile devices, printers, peripherals, and workplace technology.

• Understand basic networking concepts, connectivity troubleshooting, cabling, and network equipment.

• Demonstrate experience with ITSM tools, preferably ServiceNow, and IT asset management processes.

• Understand asset lifecycle management, inventory control, and CMDB principles.

• Communicate effectively in English and the local language.

• Work independently, prioritize effectively, and take ownership of technical issues through resolution.

• Collaborate effectively with remote IT teams, vendors, and business stakeholders.

• Maintain a professional, customer-focused approach when supporting employees and business operations.

• Hold an Associate Degree, technical diploma, or equivalent technical experience.

• Flexibility to work fully onsite (100% presential), with occasional travel to regional sites as required

**What We Offer

**

• Gain international exposure by collaborating with Global IT teams and colleagues across multiple countries.

• Develop your technical skills through hands-on experience with enterprise technologies and diverse IT environments.

• Build your career within a global organization with opportunities for professional growth and continuous learning.

• Work in a collaborative environment where your technical expertise directly contributes to business operations.

• Gain exposure to a broad range of technologies, projects, and IT functions.

• Be part of an inclusive workplace that values collaboration, diversity, and different perspectives.

• Enjoy competitive local-market compensation and benefits.

Total gross salary target range incl. variable pay: 470.000 DKK - 636.000 DKK.

**SIEM Lead in the Cyber Defense team

**As SIEM Lead, you will be the owner of our SIEM application (Splunk Enterprise Security) used by TDC NET’s Cyber Defense team. Your work will help analysts detect and investigate threats across our IT systems and Denmark’s critical telecommunications infrastructure.

**About The Job

**Your focus will be the SIEM application, its detections and the workflows analysts use every day. A dedicated engineering team in another department operates the underlying platform. You will work with that team on security data requirements and with the Head of Analysts to prioritize improvements.

Our work is guided by threat intelligence. The wider Cyber Defense team covers detection and response, threat hunting, detection engineering, incident response and forensics, penetration testing and red teaming, vulnerability management, anti-abuse and security postmaster services.

Your responsibilities

• Own the SIEM application for the Cyber Defense team, defining its roadmap and priorities with the Head of Analysts and coordinating delivery with the engineering team.

• Assess gaps in SIEM capabilities, data coverage and investigation workflows, and turn findings into a prioritized improvement plan. Track progress through measures of coverage and alert quality.

• Maintain investigation dashboards, reusable searches and security context, including threat intelligence and asset and identity information used to enrich alerts.

• Define logging and data requirements for the engineering team. Validate that delivered data contains the fields, timestamps and context needed for detection and investigation.

• Act as the technical lead for SIEM analysis during major incidents, coordinating with incident response colleagues.

• Mentor analysts in SIEM use, alert analysis and investigation techniques, and review detection content and tuning decisions with the team.

• Validate detections with the Security Testing team through attack simulations and purple team exercises and follow up on missed or incomplete alerts.

Our Cyber Defense team is Trusted Introducer certified, and our Security Testing team is CREST certified.

You will join approximately 45 colleagues in TDC NET Security, with an open, informal working culture where people share knowledge and challenge ideas.

The Cyber Defense team operates a 24/7 on-call rotation. As Senior Security Analyst, you will participate in this rotation, investigating and responding to security incidents outside normal working hours.

**About You

**You are an experienced (3-5+ years of experience) security analyst with solid practical SIEM knowledge and the ability to turn operational needs into clear priorities. You can make sound decisions with incomplete information, coordinate technical analysis under pressure and communicate findings and uncertainty clearly to both technical and non-technical colleagues.

**We Are Looking For Experience In The Following Areas

**

• Working with SIEM capabilities, data flows, integrations and application configuration in a production SOC or Cyber Defense environment.

• Taking ownership of a SIEM application, assessing gaps and defining a practical, prioritized roadmap in collaboration with analysts and platform engineers.

• Investigating incidents and hunting for threats using endpoint, identity, network and application logs, with an understanding of data quality and normalization.

• Using threat intelligence and MITRE ATT&CK to define detection requirements and identify gaps in coverage.

• Translating security needs into clear requirements for engineers and providing practical guidance to less experienced analysts.

• Understanding offensive techniques such as exploitation, privilege escalation and lateral movement, and the evidence they leave in logs.

• Using penetration tests, red team findings or purple team exercises to validate detections and close monitoring gaps.

• You must be able to maintain security clearance at HEMMELIGT (SECRET) level throughout your employment.

Experience with scripting, automation and version control is welcome.

Relevant higher education and security certifications are also welcome.

**Contact

Join us in this role where you’ll be working as a Senior Operational Technology (OT) Security Officer to strengthen the security, resilience, and compliance of Ørsted Bioenergy. In this role, you will act as a trusted security lead across OT, IT, engineering, and operations, helping protect critical systems while enabling safe, reliable, and efficient operations. Further more we are partnering with operations, engineering, maintenance, IT, and third-party vendors to ensure security controls are practical, risk-based, and compatible with operational safety and availability – and we “translate” technical cyber risk into clear business, safety, and operational impact requirements. We operate in complex, multi-site, international, or safety-critical operational environments.

**Welcome to Bioenergy

**You’ll be part of OT Security where you, together with your colleagues, will be working on Ørsted Danish powerplant. Our task is to protect the powerplants ability to produce electricity and heat against hacker attacks. So you need to understand Danish, when you’re out on the powerplants. We are a small team of 4 persons located in Jutland (Jylland) who works together and strive in helping each other in our daily tasks. As a team, we have an open and direct commutation where we discuss ideas strategy and ideas to develop and mature our solutions, so they are robust and they deal with the reality we face.

**

• leading the development and continuous improvement of OT security governance, policies, standards, and procedures

• assessing, managing, and reducing cyber risk across OT environments, including industrial control systems, SCADA, PLCs, IIoT, and related networks

• defining and supporting secure OT architecture, including network segmentation, secure remote access, asset visibility, access control, logging, monitoring, and vulnerability management

• conducting OT security risk assessments, gap analyses, and maturity reviews aligned with recognised frameworks e.g. Danish legislation “Lov om styrket Beredskab i Energisektoren”, IEC 62443, ISO 27001 and relevant regulatory requirements

• partnering with operations, engineering, maintenance, IT, and third-party vendors to ensure security controls are practical, risk-based, and compatible with operational safety and availability requirements

• driving OT security awareness and training for technical and operational teams.

**To succeed in the role, you:

**

• hold a relevant degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Cyber Security, Information Technology, Automation, or equivalent practical experience

• understand and know how to operate in ICS systems and possess understanding of 24/7 production environment

• are familiar with IT networks like, Purdue model, firewall, data diodes etc.

• are a good team player and at the same are strong on being responsible of incl. conducting your own tasks – you need to be fluent in both Danish and English language as well due to nature our stake holder landscape

• are flexible - both in terms of taking on tasks outside your comfortzone, being curious in learning new areas and assist your team in whatever tasks are needed.

Do you enjoy turning complex data into clear choices that help VELUX use resources wisely? As S&OP Specialist, you will work across functions to develop scenarios and recommendations that support senior management in making key planning decisions.

Meet your future team

You will join Global Planning – S&OP & Planning Excellence, a team that collaborates cross-functionally with Marketing, Regional Management, Supply and Finance to support connected planning processes across VELUX. The team consists of six colleagues based in Skjern and Kolding.

The S&OP Specialist is a new role in the team, introduced to ensure better alignment across functions in the planning processes.

What We Offer

As S&OP Specialist, you will support the Global S&OP process by consolidating market input, preparing scenarios and creating decision material and recommendations for senior management. You will bring structure to S&OP preparation and ensure that agreed decisions are translated into clear planning requirements.

As part of your onboarding, you will be introduced and trained in the current Demand Planning processes and tools to build your understanding of the VELUX supply chain and planning processes.

More specifically your tasks will be to:

• Ensure that worst/best case sales scenarios is agreed and aligned with the regional management in key markets and understand their assumptions, risk and opportunities.

• Support the global Demand Planning Network in coordinating market input, sales uncertainties, campaigns, allocation requirements and scenarios.

• Plan and facilitate Pre-S&OP meetings and prepare topics that require decisions.

• Develop and evaluate scenarios with Sales, Supply, Purchasing, and Finance, including implications for service, inventory, capacity, production, costs and financial performance.

• Prepare clear decision material for Global S&OP meetings, outlining alternatives, business trade-offs, risks and required decisions.

• Document decisions and follow up on actions, deadlines and outcomes, while translating agreed decisions into input for Master Planning.

This role can be based in Skjern, Kolding, Østbirk or Hørsholm and you can expect minimal traveling in Denmark and abroad.

What You Will Bring Into The Organization

You bring experience from a planning-related role and understand how decisions on demand, supply, inventory and financial priorities connect across the value chain and have translated that understanding into measurable business outcomes.

You combine curiosity and structure with a commercial mindset and business acumen; you can challenge assumptions constructively and connect planning decisions to customer needs, operational trade-offs and financial performance.

Moreover, we expect that you:

• Bring experience from Demand Planning, S&OP, Integrated Business Planning, Supply Planning, Master Planning, Sales Forecasting or Supply Chain Analysis in fast-moving consumer goods.

• Have extensive understanding of S&OP and end-to-end supply chain planning, including how planning decisions affect service, capacity, inventory and production.

• Have advanced Excel skills, experience using Power BI for analysis and reporting, and familiarity with SAP BW/BWP data structures and data extraction.

• Have the financial understanding needed to assess business cases and quantify the implications of scenarios for costs, inventory, revenue and overall business performance.

• Can establish constructive working relationships with stakeholders across functions and levels to ensure that decisions, assumptions, responsibilities and actions are transparent and followed through.

• Can translate data-based scenarios into simple, clear visualisations that enable decision makers to compare options, understand key trade-offs and make informed decisions.

**ORDERYOYO – Senior Data & AI Platform Engineer

**Remote

• Quarterly team gatherings in one of our global offices

Join OrderYOYO’s Data team to build the data pipelines and lakehouse that power executive reporting and merchant insights across our platform, and automate how we deliver finance data and AI-driven data products to the rest of the business.

You’ll own complex changes from technical design through release and production operation, working closely with the leadership team, Finance, Product and fellow engineers. Your work will improve the accuracy and reliability of our reporting, merchant insights and finance data, while reducing routine manual Finance work.

Our data platform runs in a Microsoft Azure cloud environment, and we’re moving it to Microsoft Fabric. We value transferable experience: strong Azure Databricks or Synapse engineers who can quickly develop deep Fabric expertise are encouraged to apply. This is a hands-on engineering role, not a pure architecture, BI or people-management position, and you’ll regularly design, code, troubleshoot and operate production data solutions.

**Role Mission

**Build and evolve OrderYOYO’s data platform into a single source of truth for executive reporting, merchant insights, finance automation and AI, leading the move to a modern Microsoft Fabric lakehouse. You’ll help strengthen the reliability and quality of our data in production while building AI into how we deliver data products and supporting our growing international restaurant platform.

**Core Responsibilities

**

• Design, build and operate production-grade data solutions in Microsoft Fabric across Lakehouse, Warehouse, notebooks, pipelines and related platform capabilities.

• Build and run production pipelines in Fabric, Python and PySpark that are tested and maintainable, not just notebooks.

• Design ingestion and transformation patterns that scale across multiple source systems, databases and business domains while controlling source impact, concurrency and platform cost.

• Manage Fabric capacity and cost, and retire redundant legacy layers.

• Lead migrations from legacy to modern platforms with metric parity, stakeholder sign-off, change control and safe decommissioning.

• Run the platform in production: monitoring, alerting, incident triage, root-cause analysis, data-quality checks, lineage and runbooks.

• Diagnose and resolve production issues across SQL, Spark, pipelines and semantic models, including performance degradation, data failures and capacity/resource constraints.

• Support and evolve governed semantic models and reusable metric definitions, working closely with analytics and business stakeholders to ensure performance, consistency and reliability.

• Build AI into the platform and our delivery: RAG, Azure OpenAI and agents, with prompt and version management.

• Deliver applied data science such as churn, recommendations, personalisation, fraud or risk models, and show the results.

• Work with executives, Finance, Product and engineering, and judge when to move fast, standardise, automate or hold.

**Must-have Requirements

**

• 8+ years of relevant data experience, including substantial recent hands-on data engineering or data-platform engineering responsibility in production environments.

• Demonstrated ability to independently take a data-engineering problem from requirements and technical design through implementation, production deployment, monitoring and ongoing operation.

• Deep hands-on Microsoft Fabric, or strong Synapse, Databricks or Delta experience with a clear path to Fabric.

• Strong understanding of lakehouse architecture and Delta-based data engineering, including partitioning, schema evolution, file optimisation and performance considerations.

• Expert SQL and T-SQL, including complex modelling and tuning.

• Production-grade Python or PySpark.

• Strong experience designing and implementing incremental data ingestion patterns, including approaches such as CDC, change tracking or watermarks, with reliable merge/upsert, replay and idempotent processing.

• Experience with analytical and semantic data modelling, ideally with Power BI/Fabric semantic models, including performance optimisation, governance and reusable business metrics.

• Working knowledge of Azure platform fundamentals including Azure SQL, ADLS/OneLake, Entra ID, managed identities, RBAC and Key Vault.

• A track record of leading a legacy-to-modern migration.

• Real, hands-on AI engineering beyond out-of-the-box Copilot.

• Concrete data science or ML models you delivered, with results.

**Strong-to-have Experience

**

• Strong Power BI/Fabric experience, including Direct Lake, DAX, semantic model performance tuning, incremental refresh and capacity considerations.

• Infrastructure-as-Code experience with Terraform, Bicep or equivalent tooling.

• Data platform experience in SaaS, marketplace, fintech, payments, e-commerce or multi-region businesses.

**Who We Are

**At OrderYOYO, company culture comes first. We create a positive, inclusive environment where people are trusted to do their best work and take ownership of what they build. We look for engineers who take ownership, raise risks early, explain decisions clearly, collaborate respectfully and follow through on commitments.

Our values describe what that looks like day to day:

• Passion: Adaptable and positive in a fast-moving environment, proactive about improving how things work.

• Action: Leads by example and takes the initiative rather than waiting to be asked.

• Compassion: Supports colleagues and considers the impact of decisions on merchants and teammates.

• One Team: Communicates clearly in writing and in person, stays calm under pressure and shares information openly.

We help restaurants succeed online by providing branded websites, mobile apps and tailored marketing solutions, giving them full control of their business. By removing high commission fees charged by third-party platforms, we empower restaurants to grow sustainably.

**What We Offer

**

• A salary of up to £75,000 per year (or local equivalent).

• A remote role, with quarterly in-person gatherings at one of our global offices.

• Ownership of a business-critical data and AI platform.

• A collaborative, international engineering team.

Are you ready to help shape the future of hearing care? In this role, you will identify emerging technologies and turn promising opportunities into mature concepts that can inform GN Hearing’s future solutions.

In the role of Incubation & Technology Scouting Lead in the GN Hearing R&D organization, you will connect external technology intelligence with GN Hearing’s internal capabilities to mature early opportunities into validated concepts, prototypes and well-framed development initiatives.

The Team You Will Be Part Of

You will join GN Hearing’s R&D organization, where we develop advanced hearing solutions that support people with hearing loss in everyday life. Our work brings together expertise across audiology, acoustics, electronics, mechanics, embedded software, algorithms, fitting solutions and digital services.

You will work across a broad network of technical specialists, product teams and external partners. We are curious, collaborative and practical in our approach, combining exploration with a clear focus on bringing meaningful innovations closer to product development.

Your Contribution Is Appreciated, And You Will

• Scout and assess technology opportunities by monitoring emerging technologies, companies, suppliers, research and ecosystem developments relevant to GN Hearing’s technology and product strategy.

• Build actionable technology intelligence by maintaining the opportunity roadmap, knowledge base and internal expert network, and translating internal and external signals into recommendations for R&D leadership, product management and innovation teams.

• Evaluate and mature external opportunities through early technical dialogue, partner assessments and due diligence, with appropriate consideration for confidentiality, intellectual property, data and regulatory requirements.

• Turn opportunities into development-ready concepts by leading feasibility work, proof of concepts and early prototypes, and aligning cross-functional experts around system vision, interfaces, performance targets, risks and key assumptions.

To perform well in the role, we imagine that you:

• You bring an advanced degree in a related technical field.

Our spectrometers find their way into medical devices and scientific instruments used in sustainable energy, industrial, pharmaceutical, life sciences, security, and many other applications.

• Three offices: Copenhagen, London and Iași, with customers across more than 15 countries.

Over one million Danes use Skatteguiden to understand and optimise their taxes. We automate tax tracking, surface deductions people didn't know they had, and give users the insight they need to make better financial decisions. All connected directly to the Danish tax authority. We're an independent company of around 65 people based in Copenhagen, with a 4.7-star rating and a simple mission: make financial insight accessible to everyone, not just those who can afford an accountant.

We're looking for a Head of IT who wants to build something most companies are still only talking about: AI-native IT operations. You'll own our IT function end-to-end, with the mandate, the tools, and the backing to automate as much as you can. If automating IT operations excites you, and you want room to see how far it can go, this is for you.

What you'll build

Most IT functions run on people working through admin consoles and ticket queues. We want ours to run on systems: agents, pipelines and automations that do the work, with you as their architect. Often that means connecting systems yourself: using AI to integrate one tool with another, in a way that's secure and keeps personal data where it belongs.

A few pictures of where this could lead. Which become real, and how, is your call:

- Your team is the agents you build. They handle onboarding, access, devices and support. You decide what they do alone, what needs a human, and how that changes as they earn trust.

- IT you just ask. "Maria starts Monday as a data analyst" becomes an identity, licences, groups, an enrolled laptop and Slack access. Within policy, fully logged, and nobody opened an admin console.

- No standing access for people or agents. Access is granted when it's needed, justified, logged and removed automatically. Least privilege maintains itself instead of waiting for a quarterly review.

- Every agent is governed like a colleague. AI is spreading across every team here. Each agent, in engineering and beyond, gets an identity, a scope and a lifecycle, managed as rigorously as people.

What makes this hard is also what makes it worth doing. Our users trust us with their tax and financial data, and that trust is the business. So security and privacy aren't a layer on top of this work; they're the design brief.

An agent with admin rights is a new attack surface, so its permissions must be scoped, time-bound, auditable and visible to our 24/7 security monitoring. AI must never become a path for personal data to leave our control: what a model sees, where it runs and what it retains are decisions you make and defend. And when an agent is unsure, it stops and asks a human.

We plan to grow from 65 to 100+ people over the next few years, and IT has to keep pace. Automation has helped IT scale for years, but AI changes how much of the work it can take on. That combination, not hiring, is the main lever we want to use.

What you'll own

You'll own IT end-to-end:

- Identity and access: provisioning, access rights, least privilege and licence management

- Endpoints: a fleet of mostly MacBooks, with some Windows, managed via MDM.

- Hardware: laptops, screens, peripherals and meeting-room equipment, from buying and setting up workstations for new joiners to fixing what breaks

- Network: firewall, switches and access points

- Security controls: turning security requirements into practical configurations, and supporting our compliance work

- Day-to-day operations: onboarding, offboarding, Microsoft 365, Slack and hands-on support. When a laptop won't charge, or a VPN acts up, you're the person people turn to.

- Documentation and vendors: so things don't live only in your head, and so agents have the context they need

Beyond IT itself, every team here uses AI, and agents need identities, scoped access, managed devices and the right knowledge to work with. You'll work closely with our DevOps platform team on how engineers work with agents. You'll also help define how AI is set up across the company, including how agents get the context they need without seeing more than the person they act for.

How you'll work

This is a hands-on role with real ownership. You'll make the plans, set the priorities, weigh the trade-offs, and then do the work.

The big platform choices are made at company level. We're Microsoft-centred: hosting is moving to Azure, and Entra ID is our identity provider. One stack gives us one identity plane and one automation surface, all visible to our security monitoring. If you have good arguments for doing something differently, we want to hear them. Everything below that is yours: the tools, the vendors, the priorities and how it's built.

You'll report to our CTO. He won't manage IT; you will, and he's your sparring partner on direction. You'll own the IT budget, and decisions here are fast: if a tool will help, a lean procurement process gets it in place without committees.

You'll work directly with our Head of Security & Privacy, Legal Counsel, Engineering and the rest of the business, with no one brokering it for you.

Where you'll start

You'll take ownership of a recently insourced IT function, with the opportunity to shape its foundations. You'll assess what's there and decide what to keep, change or improve, so the foundations everything else builds on are yours.

From there, the arc is roughly this:

1. Solid foundations: make the setup yours, and strong enough to build on.

2. Automate the everyday: support, onboarding and access are the first and most obvious targets.

3. Scale: agents across the company, and IT that keeps up with growth by building first.

Who we're looking for

We're open to the exact background. What matters most is how you work: you think AI-first, you have a solid IT foundation, and you use AI to go deep on whatever comes next, with the judgment to know when its answers are right.

Must-have

- You think AI-first. You use AI in your daily work and reach for it first. You've built automations or integrations with AI, ideally ones that use AI themselves, and you can show us examples.

- You learn with AI, and judge what it gives you. When you meet a technology you don't know, you use AI to get up to speed, and you know enough to tell when its suggestion is right, wrong or risky.

- Automation excites you. You see a repeated task as something to automate, and you enjoy finding out how far automation and AI can take IT.

- Solid hands-on IT experience across infrastructure, endpoints, identity and security, including working knowledge of Microsoft Entra, Intune and Microsoft 365, and of managing MacBook fleets alongside Windows.

- Solid networking skills: You can design, run, secure and monitor an office network: firewalls, switches and Wi-Fi.

- Experience somewhere security isn't an afterthought. Finance or fintech is a good example.

- A security mindset that knows when to push back and when to keep things simple. You find solutions that protect without getting in people's way.

- Comfortable with hands-on end-user support. When someone's laptop isn't charging or their VPN is playing up, you're the person they turn to. You don't consider it beneath you, and you're good at it, even while you work to make most of it disappear.

Nice-to-have

- A software engineering mindset: you treat configuration as code, use version control and review changes before they ship

- Familiarity with security frameworks such as ISO 27001

Why join us

- Define what AI-native IT looks like. Few companies have figured it out yet. You'll get to figure it out here, with full ownership and room to experiment.

- AI without a meter. The best AI models for the job, like everyone here, with no cap on token spend. We care about using tokens well, not about limiting them.

- A product that matters. More than one million Danes use what we build to understand their finances.

- Small and solid. Independent and profitable, with no VC pressure and no layers between a decision and its outcome.

- Good people. We take the work seriously without taking ourselves too seriously. The culture is professional, informal and genuinely collaborative.

Practical details

Location: Copenhagen. We're an office-first company, and it's a deliberate choice. We're moving fast, we have big ambitions, and we genuinely believe that being physically together is one of the things that makes that possible. Things move quicker when you can turn your chair and talk to someone. We want to be upfront about this so you know what to expect.

And if we're asking people to be in the office, we want it to be worth their while. We're a five-minute walk from Rådhuspladsen, stocked with everything from fruit to fizzy drinks to afternoon snacks, and lunch is at Claus Meyer's canteen just across the street, proper food, not an afterthought. If you're putting in a long day, dinner is covered too.

Salary: Competitive and based on your experience.

Reporting to: CTO

Start date: As soon as possible, ideally December 1st

The Sustainable and AI-Driven Software Development Group (SustainAI) at the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science (IMADA), University of Southern Denmark (SDU, Campus Vejle), invites applications for PhD fellowships in Computer Science, with an emphasis on Sustainable and AI-Driven Software Development.

We welcome applications from researchers interested in areas that include, but are not limited to:

• 
Sustainable and AI-Driven Software Developent, including approaches to improving the sustainability, efficiency, and reliability of software systems.

• 
Cloud and Distributed Computing, including cloud and edge computing, Internet of Things, microservices, serverless architectures, and web technologies.

The targeted starting period is Spring 2027, with room for flexibility.

Whom we are looking for

We are looking for motivated candidates interested in pursuing PhD research in Computer Science, particularly within the research areas relevant to SustainAI.

For the PhD position, applicants should possess, or be nearing completion of, an MSc degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Processing Science, Advanced-Systems Engineering, or a closely related discipline. Ideal candidates demonstrate strong academic performance, research potential, and motivation to pursue scientific research.

Experience or demonstrated interest in empirical research methods, AI-driven software engineering, software architecture, formal methods, cloud-native systems, or software sustainability is particularly relevant. However, applicants with complementary expertise that can strengthen or expand SustainAI's research activities are equally encouraged to apply.

Fluency in English is required.

Candidates who have not yet completed their qualifying degree must obtain it before taking up the respective position.

Questions?

Curious to learn more about the positions, research topics, or working environment? Please feel free to contact Professor Valentina Lenarduzzi (lenarduzzi@imada.sdu.dk) for further information.

Hosting environment

The position will be part of the Sustainable and AI-Driven Software Development Group (SustainAI) located at SDU Vejle. 

SustainAI is a research group within the Section of Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, and Programming Languages (ACP) at the University of Southern Denmark's Department of Mathematics and Computer Science (IMADA). 

SustainAI conducts research at the intersection of software engineering, artificial intelligence, and sustainability, with the ambition of advancing the development, operation, and evolution of intelligent, reliable, and sustainable software systems.

The group’s research encompasses empirical software engineering, software architecture, software quality, AI-driven software development, cloud-native technologies, and the application of emerging AI techniques to software engineering challenges.

SustainAI combines foundational and empirical research with practical applications, promoting collaboration with international academic partners, industry, and public organisations. Its activities aim to advance software engineering knowledge and practices while addressing emerging technological, environmental, and societal challenges.

The group is part of the new SDU Centre for Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence at Campus Vejle, offering opportunities for interdisciplinary research, international collaboration, and professional development.

More information about SustainAI can be found at https://sustainai.sdu.dk/. 

The Section of Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, and Programming Languages (ACP) at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is part of the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science (IMADA).

The section brings together research and education in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, programming languages, and software engineering. Its activities focus on developing intelligent, secure, reliable, and sustainable software systems, combining fundamental research with practical applications and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Research within ACP addresses topics such as AI-driven software development, software architecture and evolution, programming language technologies, formal methods, distributed computing, cybersecurity, software quality, and trustworthy AI.

The section promotes collaboration with industry, public organisations, and international research partners to address emerging technological and societal challenges. Through its research, teaching, and knowledge-transfer activities, ACP contributes to advancing the foundations and engineering practices of modern computing systems while educating the next generation of computer science professionals and researchers.

More information about the section is available at https://acp.sdu.dk/.

The section is part of the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science which offers an inclusive and international working environment with state-of-the-art facilities and strong traditions of collaboration across research groups, departments, and faculties, as well as with external organisations, including educational institutions, municipalities, and companies.

The degrees offered by the department include BSc and MSc degrees in Computer Science, a BSc degree in Artificial Intelligence, and an MSc degree in Data Science.

More information about the department can be found at https://imada.sdu.dk/.

The University of Southern Denmark (SDU) was founded in 1966 and has more than 27,000 students, almost 20% of whom are from abroad. The university has more than 3,800 employees and offers 115 study programmes across the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, health sciences, and engineering.

The positions are based at SDU Campus Vejle, part of the university's growing activities in computer science and artificial intelligence. Vejle provides an international and welcoming environment, combining an active urban centre with easy access to nature and recreational areas. Its central location in Denmark offers convenient connections to other major Danish cities and international transport hubs.
